subject: English
description: Past perfect, present perfect continuous, future perfect, conditional tenses

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: 'By the time we arrived, the train ___ already.'
questions.explanation: Two past events — earlier one in PAST PERFECT ('had left'), later in simple past ('arrived'). Pattern: 'By the time + past, past perfect had happened'. Distractor 1 — simple past loses the sequence. Distractor 3 — present perfect (mismatch with past time). Distractor 4 — simple present.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: 'She ___ at this company since 2018.'
questions.explanation: Action started in past + still continuing → PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS ('has been working'). Trigger words: SINCE, FOR. Distractor 1 — present continuous misses 'since 2018'. Distractor 3 — past continuous suggests it ended. Distractor 4 — simple present misses duration.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: 'By next year, they ___ ten years of marriage.'
questions.explanation: FUTURE PERFECT — 'will have + past participle' for an action that will be completed by a specific point in the future. Pattern: 'By + future time, will have done'. Distractor 1 — simple present. Distractor 3 — present continuous. Distractor 4 — present perfect (no future reference).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: 'If I ___ the lottery, I would buy a house.'
questions.explanation: SECOND CONDITIONAL — hypothetical/unlikely present-future. Pattern: 'If + simple past, would + base verb'. Use 'won' (subjunctive past form). Distractor 1 — first conditional (real possibility), would need 'will buy', not 'would buy'. Distractor 3 — third conditional (past unreal), would need 'would have bought'. Distractor 4 — never used after 'if' in conditionals.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: 'If she had studied harder, she ___ the exam.'
questions.explanation: THIRD CONDITIONAL — past unreal / counterfactual. Pattern: 'If + past perfect, would have + past participle'. She didn't actually study harder, so the consequence is also counterfactual: 'would have passed'. Distractor 1 — second conditional ending. Distractor 3 — simple present. Distractor 4 — first conditional ending.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: 'I ___ for two hours when he finally called me.'
questions.explanation: PAST PERFECT CONTINUOUS — action that was ongoing for a duration up to a point in the past. Pattern: 'had been + V-ing'. Two past events: long action (waiting for 2 hours) BEFORE the shorter event (he called). Distractor 1 — past continuous loses the duration sense. Distractor 3 — present perfect continuous (current relevance). Distractor 4 — simple past loses the ongoing aspect.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: 'Look! The kids ___ in the garden.'
questions.explanation: PRESENT CONTINUOUS — for actions happening RIGHT NOW. 'Look!' signals immediate observation → present continuous 'are playing'. Distractor 1 — simple present implies habitual action. Distractor 3 — past simple. Distractor 4 — present perfect (focus on result).
